2373.title: feat(number-theory): add bounded prime affine tuple operations

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preflight the translated tuple's aggregate digit bound**

When a source contains many forms, this validates each translated constant separately but never checks the `PrimeAffineTuple` aggregate limit. For example, 512 primitive forms with distinct 128-digit coefficients and constant `1`, translated by a 64-digit shift, pass this request validator because every new constant remains below 256 digits; however, their combined coefficient/constant size exceeds `MAX_AFFINE_AGGREGATE_DIGITS`, so `translated_tuple()` raises a Pydantic `ValidationError` while constructing the result. Reject this during request validation by accounting for the complete translated aggregate, so an accepted `math.run` request cannot escape as a host validation exception.

2366.title: Add exact word RSK correspondence and inverse

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject unencodable alphabet symbols before inverse execution**

When an inverse pair uses a lone surrogate such as `"\ud800"` as an alphabet symbol, `RSKTableauPair` and `RSKInverseWordRequest` accept it because `Symbol` only enforces string length, but the forward replay reaches this UTF-8 encoding and raises `UnicodeEncodeError` instead of returning a typed result. This is reachable through the native API and JSON decoders such as `json.loads`; validate that symbols are Unicode scalar strings before admitting either RSK request (or convert the encoding failure into request validation).

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not replay transient backend errors**

When the initial evaluation returns `BACKEND_ERROR` because Arb raises one of the caught exceptions, validating the emitted result later reruns Arb; if the transient failure does not recur, the replay produces `ENCLOSED` and rejects the operation's own serialized result as invalid. This makes backend-error results impossible to reliably round-trip or compose through the declared result type, so nonconclusions should be validated structurally rather than requiring the same backend failure to recur.

2350.title: feat(math): add complete canonical Nim option families

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind each NimOption to its source position**

Because `NimOption` is exported as a canonical value, this validator accepts objects that are not legal Nim moves—for example, source index `(49,)`, source size `2`, replacement size `1`, and an empty resulting position—because it never checks the indices against a source or reconstructs the resulting position. Include the source position in the value and validate the complete move relation, or keep this context-dependent row non-public so callers cannot construct mathematically invalid canonical values.
